findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe loads the per-user row with TopicUser.find_by and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If that row does not exist (logged-in user who can see the topic but has never had a topic_users record, or a category/mailing-list recipient whose row was never created), tu is nil and this raises NoMethodError. The email link then returns 500 and the notification level is not changed, so the unsubscribe action fails for exactly the people who need it. Use TopicUser.change (which inserts a row when missing) or create a muted row before updating.

findings.title: One-click unsubscribe does not stop notifications for watching or tracking users
findings.body: The email copy and the new client string both say the link stops notifications for this topic, but the action only mutes when notification_level is regular or already muted. Watching (3) and tracking (2) are greater than regular, so they are downgraded to regular instead of muted. Regular still generates reply, mention, and quote notifications, so a user who is emailed because they are watching the topic — the main case for a per-topic unsubscribe link — keeps receiving those emails after one click. The confirmation page always claims notifications have stopped, and nothing tells them they must click again to actually mute.

findings.title: Direct TopicUser save leaves notifications_reason_id nil so auto-track undoes the change
findings.body: The new action assigns notification_level and calls save! instead of TopicUser.change. change is what sets notifications_changed_at, notifications_reason_id (user_changed), and the MessageBus notification_level_change event. Leaving notifications_reason_id nil means the existing auto-track logic in TopicUser.update_last_read and TopicUser.auto_track will treat the row as never explicitly chosen and set it back to tracking once the user has viewed the topic long enough (or on the next auto_track call). A successful mute is therefore silently reverted the next time they read the topic, and other open tabs are not told the level changed.

findings.title: Unsubscribe is a cookie-authenticated GET with no recipient token
findings.body: GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe (and /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe, which 301s to the slugged URL) changes notification state with no CSRF token and no per-recipient unsubscribe key. ensure_logged_in only checks the browser session. Any site can trigger it while the victim is logged in (for example an to /t//unsubscribe); the browser sends session cookies, follows the 301, and the second request mutates state. The link also is not bound to the user who was emailed: whoever is logged in is the account that is changed, so a shared browser, staff session, or forwarded mail unsubscribes the wrong person while the recipient keeps getting mail. Email link scanners that do send cookies can apply the change without a click, and because the handler is not idempotent for watching users a second fetch drops them from regular to muted. This needs a POST (or a one-time key like the digest unsubscribe key) that identifies the recipient.

findings.title: Unsubscribe template will not be resolved by the new route
findings.body: The route is registered as a top-level topicUnsubscribe at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe (app-route-map.js.es6). Ember resolves that to the template, controller, and view names topic-unsubscribe. The controller and view were added under those names, but the template was added at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which compiles to topic/unsubscribe and is only used by a nested topic.unsubscribe route. Nothing calls renderTemplate to bridge the gap, so after the server has already changed the notification level the confirmation UI throws a missing-template error (or renders an empty outlet). The stop-notifications copy and the notification-level dropdown never appear. Move the template to templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs, or nest the route as topic.unsubscribe and move the controller/view to match.

findings.title: No coverage for the unsubscribe action or the new email link
findings.body: The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into an existing MessageBuilder example so I18n interpolation does not raise, and still only asserts that the preferences URL is in the body. Nothing asserts the new per-topic sentence or URL, and there is no request/controller spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe. The nil TopicUser crash, the watching-to-regular branch, the missing notifications_reason_id, the slug redirect, and the wrong-session GET mutation would all merge unnoticed.
